de.p: Was haben Sie letztes Wochenende gemacht?
de.en: What did you do last weekend?
de.h: Use the Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip II).

de.p: Warum lernen Sie Deutsch?
de.en: Why are you learning German?
de.h: Give two reasons with „weil“ (verb at the end).

de.p: Was müssen, können oder wollen Sie diese Woche noch erledigen?
de.en: What do you still have to, can or want to get done this week?
de.h: Use at least two modal verbs (müssen, können, wollen, sollen).

de.p: Wie war Ihre Kindheit? Erzählen Sie kurz.
de.en: What was your childhood like?
de.h: Use „war“ and „hatte“ (Präteritum).

de.p: Vergleichen Sie Zürich mit Ihrer Heimatstadt.
de.en: Compare Zurich with your hometown.
de.h: Use comparatives: größer als, teurer als, genauso … wie.

de.p: Beschreiben Sie Ihr Wohnzimmer. Was steht, liegt oder hängt wo?
de.en: Describe your living room. What stands, lies or hangs where?
de.h: Use in/auf/an/neben/über + Dativ (wo?).

de.p: Was würden Sie machen, wenn Sie ein Jahr frei hätten?
de.en: What would you do if you had a year off?
de.h: Use „würde … machen“ and „wenn ich … hätte/wäre“.

de.p: Die Heizung in Ihrer Wohnung ist kaputt. Schreiben Sie der Verwaltung und bitten Sie höflich um Hilfe.
de.en: Your heating is broken. Write to the property management and politely ask for help.
de.h: Use a formal greeting and „Könnten Sie … ?“ / „Ich wäre Ihnen dankbar, wenn …“.

de.p: Sie können nicht zur Geburtstagsfeier einer Freundin kommen. Entschuldigen Sie sich und schlagen Sie etwas anderes vor.
de.en: You can't go to a friend's birthday party. Apologise and suggest something else.
de.h: Use „leider“, a reason with „weil“ or „denn“, and „Wie wäre es mit …?“.

de.p: Beschreiben Sie Ihren Morgen, bevor Sie zur Arbeit gehen.
de.en: Describe your morning before you go to work.
de.h: Use separable verbs: aufstehen, sich anziehen, einkaufen, losfahren.

de.p: Wie erholen Sie sich nach einem langen Arbeitstag?
de.en: How do you relax after a long day at work?
de.h: Use reflexive verbs: sich ausruhen, sich entspannen, sich freuen auf.

de.p: Beschreiben Sie eine Person, die Ihnen wichtig ist.
de.en: Describe a person who is important to you.
de.h: Use at least one relative clause (der/die/das … Verb am Ende).

de.p: Was werden Sie nächstes Jahr anders machen?
de.en: What will you do differently next year?
de.h: Use „werden“ + Infinitiv.

de.p: Wie wird in Ihrem Heimatland ein großes Fest gefeiert?
de.en: How is a big holiday celebrated in your home country?
de.h: Use the passive: wird … gefeiert / gegessen / geschmückt.

de.p: Nennen Sie einen Nachteil Ihres Jobs und sagen Sie, warum Sie ihn trotzdem mögen.
de.en: Name a downside of your job and why you like it anyway.
de.h: Use „obwohl“ (verb at the end) or „trotzdem“ (verb in position 2).

de.p: Erzählen Sie von einem schönen Erlebnis, als Sie ein Kind waren.
de.en: Tell about a nice experience from when you were a child.
de.h: Use „als“ for a single event in the past.

de.p: Sollten alle Angestellten im Homeoffice arbeiten dürfen? Was ist Ihre Meinung?
de.en: Should all employees be allowed to work from home? What is your opinion?
de.h: Use „Meiner Meinung nach …“, „Ich finde, dass …“ and give a reason.

de.p: Was gefällt Ihnen an der Schweiz und was nicht so?
de.en: What do you like about Switzerland and what not so much?
de.h: Use „gefallen“ + Dativ (Mir gefällt …).

de.p: Was schenken Sie Ihrer Mutter zum Geburtstag und warum?
de.en: What are you giving your mother for her birthday, and why?
de.h: Use „jemandem (Dativ) etwas (Akkusativ) schenken“.

de.p: Ihr Paket von einem Online-Shop ist nach zwei Wochen nicht angekommen. Schreiben Sie dem Kundenservice.
de.en: Your parcel hasn't arrived after two weeks. Write to customer service.
de.h: Formal tone; say what happened (Perfekt) and what you want.

de.p: Wozu machen Sie Sport oder warum würden Sie gern mehr Sport machen?
de.en: What do you do sport for, or why would you like to do more?
de.h: Use „um … zu“ + Infinitiv or „damit“.

de.p: Sie sind in der Touristeninformation. Stellen Sie zwei höfliche Fragen.
de.en: You're at the tourist information. Ask two polite questions.
de.h: Use indirect questions: „Können Sie mir sagen, ob/wann/wo …?“ (verb at the end).

de.p: Beschreiben Sie Ihre Traumwohnung.
de.en: Describe your dream apartment.
de.h: Use adjectives before nouns: eine helle Küche, einen großen Balkon.

de.p: Seit wann wohnen Sie in Zürich, und was haben Sie vorher gemacht?
de.en: How long have you lived in Zurich and what did you do before?
de.h: Use „seit“ + Präsens and „vor … Jahren“ + Perfekt.

de.p: Sie sind zu spät zu einem Termin gekommen. Erklären Sie warum.
de.en: You were late for an appointment. Explain why.
de.h: Use „wegen des/der …“ and the Perfekt.

de.p: Was haben Sie gemacht, nachdem Sie in die Schweiz gezogen waren?
de.en: What did you do after you had moved to Switzerland?
de.h: Use „nachdem“ + Plusquamperfekt (war/hatte + Partizip).

de.p: Was haben Sie dieses Jahr noch vor?
de.en: What else are you planning to do this year?
de.h: Use „Ich habe vor, … zu …“ or „Ich versuche, … zu …“.

de.p: Ein Freund schläft seit Wochen schlecht. Geben Sie ihm zwei Ratschläge.
de.en: A friend has slept badly for weeks. Give him two pieces of advice.
de.h: Use „Du solltest …“ and „An deiner Stelle würde ich …“.

de.p: Morgen soll es den ganzen Tag regnen. Was ändern Sie an Ihren Plänen?
de.en: It's supposed to rain all day tomorrow. What do you change in your plans?
de.h: Use „deshalb“ or „deswegen“ (verb in position 2).

de.p: Auto oder öffentlicher Verkehr in Zürich: Was ist besser für Sie?
de.en: Car or public transport in Zurich: which is better for you?
de.h: Use „Ein Vorteil ist, dass …“ and „Ein Nachteil ist …“.

de.p: Was wollten Sie als Kind werden, und was mussten Sie dafür tun?
de.en: What did you want to be as a child, and what did you have to do for it?
de.h: Use wollte, musste, konnte, durfte.

de.p: Sie möchten Ihr Abo im Fitnessstudio kündigen. Schreiben Sie eine kurze E-Mail.
de.en: You want to cancel your gym membership. Write a short email.
de.h: Formal greeting and closing; „hiermit kündige ich …“, „zum nächstmöglichen Termin“.

de.p: Beschreiben Sie Ihren Arbeitsplatz und was Sie dort jeden Tag machen.
de.en: Describe your workplace and what you do there every day.
de.h: Use Präsens, prepositions of place and time expressions (morgens, meistens).

de.p: Wie hängt Ihr Schlaf mit Ihrer Laune zusammen?
de.en: How is your sleep connected to your mood?
de.h: Use „je … desto …“ with comparatives.

de.p: Was machen Sie normalerweise, während Sie mit dem Tram fahren?
de.en: What do you usually do while you ride the tram?
de.h: Use „während“ or „bevor“ (verb at the end).

de.p: Welche Sprachen sprechen Sie, und welche nicht?
de.en: Which languages do you speak, and which not?
de.h: Use „sowohl … als auch“ and „weder … noch“.

de.p: Eine Kollegin lädt Sie am Freitag zum Abendessen ein. Antworten Sie ihr.
de.en: A colleague invites you to dinner on Friday. Reply to her.
de.h: Thank her, accept, ask a question (Uhrzeit? mitbringen?).

de.p: Schreiben Sie eine kurze Bewertung über ein Restaurant, in dem Sie kürzlich waren.
de.en: Write a short review of a restaurant you went to recently.
de.h: Use the Perfekt and adjectives: lecker, freundlich, zu teuer.

de.p: Erklären Sie, wie man von Ihrer Wohnung zur nächsten Tramhaltestelle kommt.
de.en: Explain how to get from your flat to the nearest tram stop.
de.h: Use geradeaus, links/rechts abbiegen, an … vorbei, bis zur …

de.p: Erklären Sie einem neuen Kollegen, wie die Kaffeemaschine im Büro funktioniert.
de.en: Explain to a new colleague how the office coffee machine works.
de.h: Use the imperative (Sie-form or du-form): Drück …, Stellen Sie …

de.p: Erklären Sie einer Person ohne Fachwissen, was Sie beruflich machen.
de.en: Explain to a non-expert what you do for work.
de.h: Simple sentences; use „Ich analysiere …“, „Das hilft, … zu …“.

de.p: Gibt es eine Entscheidung, die Sie heute anders treffen würden? Was hätten Sie anders gemacht?
de.en: Is there a decision you'd make differently today? What would you have done differently?
de.h: Use „hätte … gemacht“ / „wäre … gegangen“.

de.p: Wie sieht ein typischer Sonntag bei Ihnen aus?
de.en: What does a typical Sunday look like for you?
de.h: Use time words (zuerst, danach, am Nachmittag) with the verb in position 2.

de.p: Wohin möchten Sie als Nächstes reisen und warum?
de.en: Where would you like to travel next and why?
de.h: Use „nach/in + Ort“ and „weil“ or „denn“.

de.p: Was tun Sie für Ihre Gesundheit?
de.en: What do you do for your health?
de.h: Use frequency adverbs: immer, oft, manchmal, selten, nie.

de.p: Sie haben eine Rechnung bekommen, die zu hoch ist. Schreiben Sie der Firma.
de.en: You received an invoice that is too high. Write to the company.
de.h: Formal; describe the problem and ask for a corrected invoice (Konjunktiv II).

de.p: Sie sind krank und können heute nicht arbeiten. Schreiben Sie Ihrem Team eine kurze Nachricht.
de.en: You are sick and can't work today. Write your team a short message.
de.h: Say why, what is urgent, and who can help (Futur / Modalverben).

de.p: Welche Jahreszeit mögen Sie am liebsten?
de.en: Which season do you like best?
de.h: Use the superlative (am liebsten) and both „weil“ and „denn“.

de.p: Erzählen Sie von Ihrem ersten Tag in einem neuen Job.
de.en: Tell about your first day at a new job.
de.h: Use Perfekt and Präteritum of sein/haben.

de.p: Sollte man Kindern schon früh ein Handy geben?
de.en: Should children get a mobile phone early on?
de.h: Give one argument for, one against, and your opinion.

de.p: Sie haben am Telefon etwas nicht verstanden. Was sagen Sie?
de.en: You didn't understand something on the phone. What do you say?
de.h: Use polite phrases: „Könnten Sie das bitte wiederholen?“, „Habe ich richtig verstanden, dass …?“

de.p: Wie stellen Sie sich Ihr Leben in zehn Jahren vor?
de.en: How do you picture your life in ten years?
de.h: Use „sich vorstellen“, „werden“ and „hoffen, dass …“.

ds.p: How do you tell whether a model is underfitting or overfitting, and what would you do in each case?
k: Compare training vs validation error (learning curves)
Underfit: more capacity/features, less regularisation
Overfit: regularise, simplify, more data, early stopping
Check data leakage before trusting a great validation score

ds.p: How would you validate a model that forecasts battery temperature 24 hours ahead?
k: Time-ordered splits / rolling-origin backtest, no shuffling
Only features available at forecast time (weather forecasts, not actuals)
Gap/embargo between train and test
Evaluate per site and per season, compare to a naive baseline

ds.p: Your PCS overheating detector fires 30 alerts a week and field engineers have started ignoring them. What do you do?
k: Measure precision using engineer feedback as labels
Tune thresholds to an agreed alert budget
Add persistence/hysteresis and severity ranking
Group related alerts, explain why each fired, work with engineers on the workflow

ds.p: Why can accuracy be misleading for rare-failure prediction, and what would you report instead?
k: Majority class dominates: predicting 'no failure' looks great
Precision/recall, PR-AUC, recall at fixed precision
Cost-weighted metrics reflecting real costs
Check calibration if probabilities drive decisions

ds.p: How would you test whether a new chiller setpoint strategy saves energy without hurting cell health?
k: Randomise by site/container or use switchback design
Primary metric (aux energy) plus guardrails (cell temperature, degradation proxies)
Control for weather: stratify or variance reduction
Power analysis, fixed duration, no peeking

ds.p: Explain a p-value to a non-technical manager, and name one common misuse.
k: Probability of data at least this extreme if there were no effect
Not the probability the hypothesis is true
Misuses: peeking, multiple testing, p-hacking
Statistical vs practical significance (effect size)

ds.p: A firmware update was rolled out to some sites but not others. How would you estimate its effect without an experiment?
k: Difference-in-differences; check parallel pre-trends
Synthetic control or matching on site characteristics
Handle staggered rollout timing
Placebo/robustness checks, watch for selection bias in which sites got it

ds.p: What are the pitfalls of interpreting SHAP or permutation feature importance?
k: Correlated features share or steal credit
Importance is not causality
Permutation importance should be on held-out data
SHAP gives local explanations; global summaries can hide interactions

ds.p: How do you monitor a model after deployment?
k: Input drift (PSI, KS) and data quality checks
Prediction distribution drift
Performance once delayed labels arrive
Alert thresholds, retraining triggers, ownership/runbook

ds.p: Telemetry from some sites has gaps. How do you handle them?
k: Understand why: comms outages may correlate with events (not random)
Short gaps: interpolate; long gaps: don't fabricate
Missingness indicators as features
Track data completeness per site and fix at source

ds.p: When would you choose gradient boosting over a neural network for tabular sensor data, and vice versa?
k: GBMs: strong default for tabular, fast, little tuning, robust
NNs: very large data, raw sequences, multimodal, transfer learning
Consider latency, edge compute, interpretability
Start with a baseline and let validation decide

ds.p: What is the practical difference between L1 and L2 regularisation?
k: L1 drives coefficients to zero: sparsity/feature selection
L2 shrinks smoothly, handles collinearity
Elastic net combines both
Features must be scaled

ds.p: Why might you group cross-validation folds by site, and what happens if you don't?
k: Rows from the same site are correlated
Random folds leak site identity, inflating scores
GroupKFold measures generalisation to new sites
Combine with time ordering when relevant

ds.p: How would you decide whether a model runs on the site controller or in the cloud?
k: Latency and safety requirements
Connectivity reliability
Compute/memory limits and model size
Updates, rollback and monitoring; hybrid options

ds.p: A senior stakeholder wants a model in two weeks that you think needs two months. How do you handle it?
k: Clarify the decision the model supports
Offer an MVP/baseline (rules, heuristic) with stated limits
Phased plan with milestones and risks
Agree success criteria together

ds.p: Why do you start with a simple baseline before building a complex model?
k: Sets the bar complexity must beat
Sanity-checks the pipeline and data
Sometimes good enough and cheaper to run
Makes the value of extra complexity visible

ds.p: How do you choose between MAE, RMSE and MAPE for a forecast?
k: RMSE punishes large errors more
MAE is robust and in original units
MAPE breaks near zero and is asymmetric
Pick by the cost of errors; compare with a naive skill score

ds.p: Why would you produce prediction intervals instead of a single forecast, and how?
k: Decisions under risk need ranges (dispatch, maintenance)
Quantile regression, conformal prediction, ensembles
Evaluate coverage and pinball loss
Communicate intervals clearly

ds.p: What features would you use to predict battery state of health?
k: Throughput / equivalent full cycles, depth of discharge
Time at high SOC (calendar ageing)
Temperature exposure (Arrhenius-type effect)
C-rate, age; physics-informed features from BMS data

ds.p: When would you combine a physics model with machine learning, and how?
k: Limited data or need to extrapolate
Respect physical constraints (energy/thermal balance)
Grey-box: ML models the residual of a physics model
More interpretable and trusted by engineers

ds.p: How is battery state of charge usually estimated, and where can data science help?
k: Coulomb counting drifts over time
OCV–SOC correction at rest
Kalman/EKF fuses model and measurements
DS: detect SOC jumps, cell imbalance, calibration issues

ds.p: How would you detect one PCS running hotter than its peers without labelled data?
k: Expected temperature given load and ambient (residual)
Compare to peer units at the same site/time
Robust z-scores, persistence before alerting
Account for seasonality and operating mode

ds.p: How do you make data science code production-ready?
k: Modular package, not notebooks
Unit and data tests, CI
Pinned environments, versioned data and models
Logging, type hints, code review

ds.p: How do you make an experiment reproducible months later?
k: Track parameters, metrics, artifacts (e.g. MLflow)
Version or snapshot the data
Lock the environment, fix seeds
Config files instead of hard-coded values

ds.p: Your analysis needs a year of 1-second telemetry from 100 sites. How do you approach it?
k: Push aggregation to the database (time buckets, downsampling)
Partition by time and site, columnar formats like Parquet
Process incrementally / in chunks or with Spark/Dask
Only pull raw resolution where needed

ds.p: How would you design storage for high-frequency sensor data across many sites?
k: Time-partitioned tables (e.g. hypertables), compression
Retention policy plus downsampled rollups
Index on site, signal, time
Trade-offs of long vs wide schemas

ds.p: How do you deal with outliers in sensor data?
k: Separate sensor errors from real events
Physical limits and domain rules
Robust statistics/models
Don't blindly drop them: they may be what you're looking for

ds.p: How do you tune hyperparameters without fooling yourself?
k: Start from sensible defaults
Random or Bayesian search within a budget
Proper validation (nested CV / untouched test set)
Early stopping; beware overfitting the validation set

ds.p: How do you help a junior data scientist grow?
k: Pair on problem scoping
Code reviews that explain the why
Ownership of a well-scoped project
Regular feedback, chances to present

ds.p: Several teams ask you for analyses at once. How do you prioritise?
k: Impact vs effort, aligned with business goals
Make trade-offs visible to stakeholders
Say no or later with reasons
Reduce repeat requests with self-serve tools

ds.p: How do you present an uncertain result to executives?
k: Lead with the decision and recommendation
Ranges or scenarios instead of false precision
What would change the conclusion
Simple visuals, no jargon

ds.p: A model in production made bad predictions for a week. How do you handle the post-mortem?
k: Blameless; build a timeline
Root cause: data, drift, bug or design
Quantify impact
Fixes plus new monitoring/tests; share learnings

ds.p: How do you know whether clusters you found are meaningful?
k: Internal metrics (silhouette) and stability across runs/samples
Domain interpretability
Actionability for the business
Compare different k and methods

ds.p: When is PCA useful, and what are its drawbacks?
k: Correlated features, compression, visualisation, denoising
Scale features first
Components are hard to interpret
Linear only; variance is not always what matters

ds.p: When would you use a Bayesian approach in practice?
k: Small data where prior knowledge helps
Full uncertainty for decisions
Hierarchical models to pool across sites
Costs: computation, choosing and explaining priors

ds.p: What problems does multicollinearity cause, and when does it matter?
k: Unstable coefficients and inflated standard errors
Detect with correlations or VIF
Matters for interpretation more than prediction
Fix: regularise, combine or drop features

ds.p: How would you model time until a component fails?
k: Survival analysis handles censored units still running
Kaplan–Meier, Cox, Weibull
Covariates such as temperature or load
Outputs feed maintenance planning

ds.p: You have very few labelled failures. How do you still build a useful detector?
k: Unsupervised or semi-supervised methods
Weak labels from maintenance logs and thresholds
Active learning with field engineers
Fault injection/simulation, transfer across sites

ds.p: How would you frame chiller setpoint control as an optimisation problem?
k: Objective: auxiliary energy cost plus degradation cost
Constraints: temperature limits and safety
Thermal model plus load and weather forecasts
Solve with MPC or dynamic programming; validate safely

ds.p: Why might model predictive control beat a fixed schedule?
k: Uses forecasts of load and weather
Re-optimises every step with fresh data
Handles constraints explicitly
Needs a good model and enough compute

ds.p: Why does probability calibration matter, and how do you check it?
k: Probabilities drive thresholds and expected-cost decisions
Reliability diagram, Brier score
Platt scaling or isotonic regression
Boosted trees and NNs are often miscalibrated

ds.p: How do you decide how long an experiment needs to run?
k: Minimum effect size worth detecting
Variance of the metric, alpha and power
Small effects need much more data
Fix duration up front; variance reduction helps

ds.p: What is training-serving skew and how do you prevent it?
k: Features computed differently in training and production
Share one feature code path / feature store
Point-in-time correct training data
Monitor live feature distributions vs training

ds.p: How do you trade off model interpretability against accuracy?
k: Depends on risk, safety and who must trust it
Prefer the simple model when performance is close
Explainability tools for complex models
Field engineers' trust affects adoption

ds.p: What automatic data-quality checks would you put on a telemetry pipeline?
k: Schema and type checks
Physical ranges, units, duplicates
Freshness and completeness per site
Alerts with owners when checks fail

ds.p: How do you handle daily and yearly seasonality in temperature data?
k: Decomposition (STL) or Fourier terms
Calendar and time-of-day features
Weather covariates explain much of it
Check residuals for leftover patterns

ds.p: A model trained on sites in a mild climate performs badly in a hot one. Why, and what do you do?
k: Covariate shift: conditions outside training range
Different operating regimes
Climate-specific features/layers, physics features
Evaluate per climate; collect targeted data

ds.p: When does ensembling help, and what does it cost?
k: Bagging reduces variance, boosting reduces bias
Stacking diverse models
Costs: complexity, latency, interpretability
Gain is small if models make the same errors

ds.p: What kinds of technical debt are specific to ML systems?
k: Glue code and pipeline jungles
Hidden feedback loops
Undeclared consumers of model outputs
Config and data dependency debt; fix with ownership, tests, monitoring

ds.p: Describe a project you're proud of in two or three sentences.
k: Context and the problem
Your specific contribution
Quantified impact
A trade-off or what you'd do differently

ds.p: Your model recommends running batteries closer to their limits. How do you make sure it stays safe?
k: Hard limits enforced outside the model
Conservative margins and uncertainty
Staged rollout, human sign-off
Monitoring with fast rollback

ds.p: Explain gradient boosting simply.
k: Trees added one after another
Each new tree fits the remaining errors (gradients)
Learning rate shrinks each step
Depth, min samples, subsampling regularise it

ds.p: For a thermal-runaway early warning, how do you balance false positives and false negatives?
k: Missed events are catastrophic, so favour recall
Tiered alerts to limit fatigue
Put numbers on the costs of each error
Set the threshold from expected cost

ds.p: How do you work effectively with field service engineers on a data project?
k: Involve them from problem definition
Use their knowledge as labels and features
Feedback loop built into the tools they use
Explainable outputs; visit sites
